test_tags.title: System/Light/Dark switch changes tokens on every screen, dark avoids pure black/white surfaces, the choice persists, default is Light, reload is zero-flash and System follows the OS live

implementation_order.rationale: FIRST: the two CSS custom-property token sets (light on :root, dark on html[data-theme=dark], @media prefers-color-scheme scoped to no-explicit-data-theme), apply_theme (AF-61), persist_theme (AF-62) and the pre-paint restore bootstrap (AF-63) land before any screen restructure so every later surface ships already token-driven — no screen ever hard-codes a color that would then need re-theming. All three AFs are browser-side with no server-AF dependencies (localStorage, matchMedia, head bootstrap are platform facilities), so nothing blocks them at position 1. Gate: TC-111 (LOCAL) exercises the whole theme contract — token switch on all six screens, dark palette constraints, persistence, default Light, zero-flash and live System follow — against this layer alone.

test_tags.title: Sidebar renders exactly the six D38 navigation labels and 'Month Grid' is absent from nav
Portfolio tabs switch between My Holdings and Payouts; Holdings columns match FR-53 and Watchlist columns match the FR-56 candidates whitelist

implementation_order.rationale: SECOND: the shell becomes the six-label D38 nav (Month Grid renamed to Portfolio; Reports/Print loses its sidebar slot) and the Portfolio screen gains its two tabs through portfolio_tab_switch (AF-64) — My Holdings registry with the exact FR-53 columns and the retained D33 drawer, Payouts as the month grid. Depends on entry 1 (the restructured chrome renders through the new token layer) and on the pre-existing shell/query foundations (AF-30, AF-52/AF-54 surfaces) — all earlier waves, no back-edge. This entry establishes the surfaces that entries 3-5 populate. Gates: TC-105 (nav labels, 'Month Grid' absent) and TC-106 (tab round-trip + Holdings column list + Watchlist whitelist assertions), both LOCAL.

test_tags.title: Portfolio tabs switch between My Holdings and Payouts; Holdings columns match FR-53 and Watchlist columns match the FR-56 candidates whitelist
Add Position auto-calculates tenure in whole months from the date range and rejects credit day 0 and 32
D15 lock rejects a duplicate company while On-going or Danger, allows re-buy after Matured, and the re-buy restarts the lifecycle
New installation starts empty — no sample rows on any screen

implementation_order.rationale: THIRD: the Watchlist becomes candidates-only (FR-56 whitelist — Invested/Received/Next Payout/health stripped, + Add Candidate stays) and both position-creation funnels land together because they share ONE lock routine: add_position (AF-65, in Portfolio > My Holdings — tenure auto-calc, credit day 1..31, shared AF-39 D15 check) and move_to_portfolio (AF-66, candidate -> Held, same AF-39 check). Depends on entry 2 (Add Position lives on the My Holdings tab; the whitelist applies inside the new shell) and on strictly earlier AFs AF-39 (lock, W2 addendum v1) and AF-50 (date/tenure, W1 addendum v2). The whitelist column assertions ride TC-106 (shared with entry 2 — one case spans both entries' surfaces); TC-112 gates first-run emptiness here because these creation flows are the ONLY way rows enter the product. Gates: TC-106 (whitelist half), TC-107 (tenure/credit-day), TC-108 (lock lifecycle incl. re-buy after Matured), TC-112 (fresh install empty) — all LOCAL.

test_tags.title: Payouts rows auto-sort Danger, On-going..., Matured... and future months are never rendered

implementation_order.rationale: FOURTH: payment health comes alive off the Payouts grid — derive_payment_health (AF-67: read-time derivation from the credit-day grid entry: paid on time -> On-going, no entry on the credit day -> Danger same day, tenure end -> Matured) then sort_payouts_rows (AF-68: Danger top, On-going next, Matured bottom with automatic re-sort; month columns stop at the current month). Depends on entry 2 (the Payouts tab must exist to derive from and sort within) and on earlier AF-14 (status engine arithmetic); intra-entry order: AF-67 before AF-68 (the sorter consumes per-row health). Gate: TC-110 (LOCAL) — mixed-status order, automatic re-sort on health change, no future month columns.

test_tags.title: DOM renders Received and Matured; Returned and Completed never render while engine values stay unchanged

implementation_order.rationale: FIFTH: render_label (AF-69) installs the display-only mapping Returned -> Received and Completed -> Matured at the render layer, after every surface that shows those strings exists (registry headers, Payouts chips, drawer, dashboard, legend from entries 2-4) so one mapping covers them all consistently and no surface can show the old face. Pure presentation: no engine, query or storage dependency — it must simply postdate the surfaces it rewrites. Gate: TC-109 (LOCAL) — DOM greps for the forbidden strings on every surface plus a database round-trip proving the stored engine value is still 'Completed'.

test_tags.title: Theme switcher renders in the header and in Settings > Appearance with the same three modes and stays in sync

implementation_order.rationale: LAST: wire the visible theme controls — the header switcher and the Settings > Appearance section — onto the entry-1 layer (apply_theme AF-61, persist_theme AF-62, restore/pre-selection AF-63): exactly System/Light/Dark labels on both surfaces, one stored choice driving both, active state synced after every selection and after reload. Placed last because the polish surfaces span every screen of the restructured shell (entries 2-5): the switcher lives in the header chrome and Settings, and both must reflect a fully restructured nav/tabs/whitelist/payouts/labels build so the control never points at a screen mid-restructure. Gate: TC-113 (LOCAL) — placement on both surfaces, identical mode sets, cross-sync and persisted pre-selection. Token-level behavior stays gated by TC-111 at entry 1.
